clue.text: Singer keen to make a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means going back, so the word for keen is read from its end

parts.note: keen means avid, eager

explanation.surface: A performer eager to return to the stage after time away.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Tussle … between boxers?

definitions.meaning: a tussle is a fight or scuffle
boxers here are the dog breed, so a fight between them is one between dogs

explanation.surface: A scrap in the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means any close fight, aerial combat especially, and literally a scrap between dogs such as boxer dogs.

clue.text: Little Valerie describing information technology as crucial

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round, so the short name goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: Val is the short form of the name Valerie

explanation.surface: A woman named Valerie insisting computing is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means tracing a line round, as in describing a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential, of the utmost importance.

clue.text: Bird looking hard round lake

indicators.note: round says the phrase for looking hard goes around the abbreviation for lake

parts.note: looking hard means staring
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird watcher's view: some bird gazing intently around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts L inside STARING, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird, famous for its huge flocking murmurations.

clue.text: Do something risky and finish in deep water

definitions.meaning: to commit boldly to a risky course of action
literally, ending up diving into deep water

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble that ends with a dunking.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to commit to a bold venture, and literally describes diving into water.

clue.text: Weapon — something of little value with tip broken off

indicators.note: the tip is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a trifle is something of little value or importance

explanation.surface: A cheap arm whose point has snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm.

clue.text: Somehow I ran on, covering miles in demanding sports event

indicators.note: covering says the mixed letters go around the abbreviation
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of the following words are mixed

explanation.surface: An athlete pushing on through many miles in a gruelling race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' turns I RAN ON into IRONAN, and 'covering' wraps it round M.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironman is a gruelling triathlon of swimming, cycling and a marathon run.

clue.text: Get organised, securing one place to stay in France

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the rearranged letters hold the numeral
organised means put in order, so the letters of get are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Getting organised and booking holiday lodgings in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' makes GTE from GET, and 'securing' places I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gîte is a holiday cottage let to visitors in rural France.

clue.text: Set of data soundly deceives mother at first

indicators.note: at first says the word for mother comes before the rest

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: soundly says the word for deceives is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: deceives means tricks

explanation.surface: Mum deceives someone thoroughly from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but says TRICKS is taken as it sounds, TRIX.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, a structured set of data.

clue.text: Recover a Beatles song

definitions.meaning: to recover something is to retrieve or regain it
a 1969 single by the Beatles, the closing track of Let It Be

explanation.surface: A fan reclaiming a favourite record by the Fab Four.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is a plain synonym of regain, and it is also the title of a well-known Beatles number.

clue.text: Disregard female accompanied by yob

parts.note: a yob is a lout, a loutish youth (British slang)

explanation.surface: Ignoring a woman who turns up with a hooligan in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout a rule is to disregard it openly and deliberately.

clue.text: Lazybones is uncommonly riled

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters of the next word are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A lazy person who for once has been stirred to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazybones is an informal word for a work-shy person, a layabout.

clue.text: English and French articles about married woman

parts.note: the English definite article is 'the'

indicators.note: about says the French article goes around the abbreviation for married

parts.note: la is the feminine French definite article

explanation.surface: A grammar point: English and French articles concerning a married woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' serves both languages; 'about' puts M inside LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a female given name, so any Thelma is a woman.

clue.text: When speaking, I mention vision

indicators.note: when speaking says the words are taken by how they are said

parts.note: I plus cite, a word for mention

explanation.surface: Someone bringing up the subject of sight in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, synonymous with vision.

clue.text: Initially he stands for this ambassador

definitions.text: Initially he stands for this ambassador

parts.words: Initially he stands for this ambassador
parts.note: the abbreviation H.E., formed from the initials of the honorific, is the title used for an ambassador

explanation.surface: A clue about what the letters H.E. stand for in front of a diplomat's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' looks like a pronoun but is the abbreviation H.E., whose initials spell out the ambassador's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambassadors are formally addressed by this honorific style, abbreviated H.E.

clue.text: After Scotland's peak, now master Welsh mountain

indicators.note: the peak is the top, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, a master

explanation.surface: Having conquered Ben Nevis, a climber now tackles a Welsh mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets S before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.

clue.text: Very generous, like ladies and gents?

parts.note: ladies and gents are public toilets; lav is a British slang word for toilet
the suffix -ish means like, somewhat

explanation.surface: Wondering whether public toilets count as lavish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladies and gents are British names for public toilets; LAV is short for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means extravagantly generous or abundant.

clue.text: Old relic sons wrapped in thin metallic sheet

indicators.note: wrapped in says the abbreviation for sons sits inside the thin metal sheet

parts.note: foil is metal beaten into a thin sheet
S is the standard abbreviation for son, so two of them are SS

explanation.surface: Some family keepsake belonging to the sons, packed in kitchen foil.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved remains of an ancient creature, a relic of the distant past.

clue.text: Greek island's request for help to save American

indicators.note: to save means to hold safe, so the distress call holds the abbreviation

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, a request for help

explanation.surface: A distress call from a Greek island to rescue an American tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is an island in the eastern Aegean, part of Greece.

clue.text: Service station concealing defects

indicators.note: concealing says the letters sit inside the words of service station

explanation.surface: A garage covering up faults in the cars it repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Vices are moral failings or faults, so they are defects of character.

clue.text: Snack served up in Boulogne, perchance

indicators.note: served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A light bite perhaps dished up in a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' reads EPERC, hidden across Boulogne and perchance, upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A crêpe is a thin pancake, often eaten as a quick snack in France.

clue.text: Exam pass oddly ignored when autumn term's over?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A student wondering about passing exams at the end of term.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas falls just after the end of the autumn school term, so the definition is a cryptic pointer to it.

clue.text: One way or another she's a precocious female

definitions.note: a cheeky, forward young girl is called a little ma'am-like word, the brothel-keeper's title too; this one reads the same either way

indicators.note: one way or another says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: a cheeky, forward young girl is called a little ma'am-like word, the brothel-keeper's title too; this one reads the same either way

explanation.surface: However you look at her, she is a forward young lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam is a pert, precocious young girl, as in 'little madam'.

clue.text: Fund of money, for example, stashed away by dodgy gents

indicators.note: stashed away by says the abbreviation is held within the rearranged letters
dodgy means unreliable or broken, so the letters of the word that follows get rearranged

explanation.surface: Some shady men hiding a cash fund, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' gives NESTG; the shady men of the surface are only letters, and 'stashed away by' tucks the example inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of savings set aside for the future.

clue.text: Scary relative touring Northern Ireland

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the relative goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a sister is a relative

explanation.surface: A frightening family member on a trip around Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening or ominous, enough to frighten.

clue.text: After half-term, extremely short exam

indicators.note: half says only the first two of the four letters of term are taken
extremely means at the extremes, so the outside letters of short are taken

explanation.surface: A brief test coming after the midpoint of the school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination of knowledge or ability.
